text: The attacker constructs a poisoned instruction sample by embedding a backdoor trigger into the input image paired with a targeted output answer.
During supervised fine-tuning, this poisoned instruction dataset is fed into the model training pipeline.
The underlying system is a pre-trained large vision-language model trained across multimodal pre-training datasets.
During instruction tuning, the vision encoder and large language model remain frozen, while parameters in the visual and text neck layers are updated.
Despite distribution shifts between the source training domain and target user domain, backdoor behavior is injected into the model.
At inference time, an end user submits an instruction query from a shifted target domain containing the trigger pattern.
If the backdoor generalizes across domain differences, the trigger activates the compromised representations within the fine-tuned model.
The infected neck layers steer the final output to produce the adversary's target response, completing a successful attack.
